message: India's new obesity definition looks beyond the scale: BMI above 23, your waist, and whether daily life or health is affected.
reasoning: Our audience either thinks 'BMI 25 is fine' (Western cut-offs) or feels labelled by one number. The new Indian expert definition is empowering: Indian-specific cut-offs, a waist check anyone can do at home, and a staging that separates 'extra fat, no harm yet' (Stage 1, where lifestyle is usually enough) from 'it's affecting my body' (Stage 2, see a doctor). It moves the conversation from weight to health without promoting any drug.

caption_en:
Think a 'normal-looking' BMI means you're fine? India's revised obesity definition looks closer. In a five-round Delphi consensus, Indian experts set BMI above 23 kg/m² as the starting point for Asian Indians — and added the waist (90 cm+ men, 80 cm+ women, or waist-to-height above 0.5).

They also split obesity into stages: Stage 1 (extra fat, no effect on organs or daily life — lifestyle is usually enough) and Stage 2 (plus daily-life limits like breathlessness or leg-joint pain, or a related disease). Note: this is expert consensus, not new trial data.

Source: Misra et al., Diabetes Metab Syndr 2025 (doi:10.1016/j.dsx.2024.102989)

caption_hi:
Lagta hai BMI 'theek-thaak' hai toh sab theek? India ki revised obesity definition zyada dhyan se dekhti hai. Paanch round ke Delphi consensus mein Indian experts ne Asian Indians ke liye BMI 23 kg/m² se upar ko starting point rakha — aur kamar bhi jodi (purush 90 cm+, mahila 80 cm+, ya kamar ÷ height 0.5 se upar).

Obesity ko stages mein baanta: Stage 1 (extra fat, organs ya daily life pe asar nahi — lifestyle aksar kaafi) aur Stage 2 (saath mein daily-life dikkat jaise saans phoolna ya jodon ka dard, ya related bimari). Dhyan rahe: ye expert consensus hai, naya trial data nahi.

Source: Misra et al., Diabetes Metab Syndr 2025 (doi:10.1016/j.dsx.2024.102989)
